findings.title: Manager dashboard lacks one-click PDF export of team engagement summary
findings.description: Office managers can view per-practice engagement trend lines on the manager dashboard but have no way to export the view; the only option is to screenshot or manually retype numbers for monthly regional-director meetings. This manual step causes wrong date ranges and typo'd numbers, so regional directors sometimes see mismatched figures for the same practice, damaging trust in the program. Customer wants a dashboard button that outputs a formatted PDF of the manager's own team summary with the selected date range baked in, so it can be dropped into slides/emails without manual recreation. Across 42 practices/office managers this happens monthly.
findings.quote: What I want — what all forty-two of them want, and they've told me so loudly — is a button on the manager dashboard that spits out their team's engagement summary as a PDF.
findings.severity_reason: Manual screenshot/retype of dashboard numbers across 42 practices produces mismatched figures that reach regional directors, undermining trust in engagement data used for real decisions; no self-serve export exists.
findings.match_note: Same capability requested — one-click PDF export of the manager dashboard's team engagement summary — as PROJ-118 (Export team engagement summary as PDF from the manager dashboard).

findings.title: Customer accepts vendor-run monthly manual export as stopgap for missing PDF export
findings.description: As a stopgap for the missing self-serve PDF export (see line 24 finding), the rep offered to manually build and send a monthly per-practice export (PDF plus a spreadsheet summary tab) using a practice-to-region mapping the customer will supply, targeted for delivery by the 1st of each month to precede the customer's first-week regional meetings. The customer accepted this as a relief but it is an internal service workaround, not a product change.
findings.quote: That would genuinely take a headache off my plate. What do you need from me to set it up?
findings.severity_reason: This is a manual, vendor-side stopgap for the already-logged export gap, not a separate product defect or request.
findings.match_note: Workaround tied directly to the PDF export request raised at line 24; not filed as its own issue per instructions.

findings.title: Unsolicited positive feedback on existing dark mode feature
findings.description: Customer explicitly frames this as 'not really a complaint' and reports that younger hygienist staff enjoy the mobile app's dark mode, saying it makes the app 'not feel like a work thing.' No defect, gap, or change is requested; mobile app is otherwise reported as fine with no issues.
findings.quote: I just wanted to say the dark mode you added a while back was a hit with the younger hygienists.
findings.severity_reason: Positive, unsolicited feedback on an already-shipped feature (PROJ-102); no change requested.
findings.match_note: Praise only, not a request; PROJ-102 (Dark mode) is already Shipped and nothing further is being asked.

findings.title: No issues reported with coaches or coach-reassignment workflow
findings.description: Customer reports coaches overall are great; one coach was not a fit for two members and the reassignment through the product was smooth and quick ('clicked the change and picked a new coach'). Customer explicitly states there is nothing to raise here. No defect or feature gap identified.
findings.quote: Coaches are great. We had one who wasn't a fit for a couple of members and the reassignment was smooth, no drama.
findings.severity_reason: Positive feedback confirming the reassignment workflow worked as intended; no defect or request raised.
findings.match_note: No corresponding catalogue issue; topic is explicitly closed out by the customer as a non-issue.
